sanskrit: nedānīm atinirbandhaṃ śoke kartum ihārhasi yad āha bhagavān vyāsas tat kuruṣva nṛpottama
english: It is not fitting now, O best of kings, to persist so stubbornly in grief: whatever the venerable Vyāsa has told you, do that.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇās tvāṃ mahābāho bhrātaraś ca mahaujasaḥ parjanyam iva gharmārtā āśaṃsānā upāsate
english: The brāhmaṇas, O mighty-armed one, and your brothers of vast vigor, wait upon you full of expectation, as men scorched by heat await the rain-cloud.

sanskrit: hataśiṣṭāś ca rājānaḥ kṛtsnaṃ caiva samāgatam cāturvarṇyaṃ mahārāja rāṣṭraṃ te kurujāṅgalam
english: The kings who survived the slaughter, and the whole of the four orders gathered together, and your realm of Kurujāṅgala, O great king—all look to you.

sanskrit: priyārtham api caiteṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām niyogād asya ca guror vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: If only to please these high-souled brāhmaṇas, and at the command of this teacher Vyāsa of measureless splendor,

sanskrit: suhṛdāṃ cāsmad ādīnāṃ draupadyāś ca paraṃtapa kuru priyam amitraghna lokasya ca hitaṃ kuru
english: and of your friends, beginning with me, and of Draupadī, O scorcher of foes—do what they wish, O slayer of enemies, and work the welfare of the world.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu kṛṣṇena rājā rājīvalocanaḥ hitārthaṃ sarvalokasya samuttasthau mahātapāḥ
english: Thus addressed by Kṛṣṇa, the lotus-eyed king of great austerity rose up for the good of all the world.

sanskrit: so 'nunīto naravyāghro viṣṭaraśravasā svayam dvaipāyanena ca tathā devasthānena jiṣṇunā
english: That tiger among men was entreated in person by Viṣṭaraśravas, and by Dvaipāyana, and likewise by Devasthāna and by Jiṣṇu,

sanskrit: etaiś cānyaiś ca bahubhir anunīto yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vyajahān mānasaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃtāpaṃ ca mahāmanāḥ
english: and entreated by these and many others, the high-minded Yudhiṣṭhira cast off the sorrow of his heart and his anguish.

sanskrit: śrutavākyaḥ śrutanidhiḥ śrutaśravyaviśāradaḥ vyavasya manasaḥ śāntim agacchat pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: A hearer of counsel, a treasury of sacred learning, skilled in what is heard and worthy to be heard, the son of Pāṇḍu resolved himself and attained peace of mind.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā nakṣatrair iva candramāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ puraskṛtya svapuraṃ praviveśa ha
english: Encircled by them like the moon by the constellations, the king, placing Dhṛtarāṣṭra before him, entered his own city.

sanskrit: pravivikṣuḥ sa dharmajñaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ arcayām āsa devāṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Wishing to enter, that knower of dharma, Yudhiṣṭhira son of Kuntī, paid worship to the gods and to the brāhmaṇas by the thousand.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ navaṃ śubhraṃ kambalājinasaṃvṛtam yuktaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir gobhiḥ pāṇḍuraiḥ śubhalakṣaṇaiḥ
english: Then a new, gleaming chariot, draped with woolen blankets and antelope hides, yoked to sixteen white oxen marked with auspicious signs—

sanskrit: mantrair abhyarcitaḥ puṇyaiḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ āruroha yathā devaḥ somo 'mṛtamayaṃ ratham
english: honored with holy hymns and praised by the great sages, he mounted it as the god Soma mounts his chariot made of nectar.

sanskrit: jagrāha raśmīn kaunteyo bhīmo bhīmaparākramaḥ arjunaḥ pāṇḍuraṃ chatraṃ dhārayām āsa bhānumat
english: Bhīma of terrible prowess, son of Kuntī, took up the reins, while Arjuna held aloft the white, sun-bright parasol.

sanskrit: dhriyamāṇaṃ tu tac chatraṃ pāṇḍuraṃ tasya mūrdhani śuśubhe tārakārājasitam abhram ivāmbare
english: And that white parasol held above his head shone forth, pale as the lord of stars, like a cloud in the sky.

sanskrit: cāmaravyajane cāsya vīrau jagṛhatus tadā candraraśmiprabhe śubhre mādrīputrāv alaṃkṛte
english: And the two heroes, the sons of Mādrī, splendidly adorned, then took up his two yak-tail fans, gleaming white with the radiance of moonbeams.

sanskrit: te pañca ratham āsthāya bhrātaraḥ samalaṃkṛtāḥ bhūtānīva samastāni rājan dadṛśire tadā
english: Those five brothers, fully adorned, mounted upon the chariot, then appeared, O king, like the five elements all together.

sanskrit: āsthāya tu rathaṃ śubhraṃ yuktam aśvair mahājavaiḥ anvayāt pṛṣṭhato rājan yuyutsuḥ pāṇḍavāgrajam
english: Mounting a gleaming chariot yoked to swift horses, Yuyutsu, O king, followed behind the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: rathaṃ hemamayaṃ śubhraṃ sainyasugrīvayojitam saha sātyakinā kṛṣṇaḥ samāsthāyānvayāt kurūn
english: Mounting a bright golden chariot yoked to Saiṇya and Sugrīva, Kṛṣṇa, together with Sātyaki, followed the Kurus.

sanskrit: narayānena tu jyeṣṭhaḥ pitā pārthasya bhārata agrato dharmarājasya gāndhārīsahito yayau
english: And the eldest, the father of Pārtha, O Bhārata, went on in a palanquin borne by men, in front of the Dharma-king, in the company of Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: kurustriyaś ca tāḥ sarvāḥ kuntī kṛṣṇā ca draupadī yānair uccāvacair jagmur vidureṇa puraskṛtāḥ
english: And all the women of the Kurus, Kuntī and Kṛṣṇā Draupadī, went in conveyances high and low, with Vidura at their head.

sanskrit: tato rathāś ca bahulā nāgāś ca samalaṃkṛtāḥ pādātāś ca hayāś caiva pṛṣṭhataḥ samanuvrajan
english: Then chariots in multitude and adorned elephants, foot-soldiers and horses too, followed along behind.

sanskrit: tato vaitālikaiḥ sūtair māgadhaiś ca subhāṣitaiḥ stūyamāno yayau rājā nagaraṃ nāgasāhvayam
english: Then, praised with eloquent words by panegyrists, bards, and minstrels, the king went on toward the city named after the elephant.

sanskrit: tat prayāṇaṃ mahābāhor babhūvāpratimaṃ bhuvi ākulākulam utsṛṣṭaṃ hṛṣṭapuṣṭajanānvitam
english: That procession of the mighty-armed one was without compare on earth, thronging and tumultuous and unrestrained, thronged with people glad and well-fed.

sanskrit: abhiyāne tu pārthasya narair nagaravāsibhiḥ nagaraṃ rājamārgaś ca yathāvat samalaṃkṛtam
english: For Pārtha's coming, the city and the royal road were duly decked out by the men who dwelt in the city.

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇa ca mālyena patākābhiś ca vedibhiḥ saṃvṛto rājamārgaś ca dhūpanaiś ca sudhūpitaḥ
english: The royal road was hung with white garlands, with banners and altar-platforms, and richly perfumed with incense.

sanskrit: atha cūrṇaiś ca gandhānāṃ nānāpuṣpaiḥ priyaṅgubhiḥ mālyadāmabhir āsaktai rājaveśmābhisaṃvṛtam
english: And the royal palace was wreathed about with powders of fragrant scents, with manifold flowers and priyaṅgu blossoms, and with hanging strings of garlands.

sanskrit: kumbhāś ca nagaradvāri vāripūrṇā dṛḍhā navāḥ kanyāḥ sumanasaś chāgāḥ sthāpitās tatra tatra ha
english: And at the city gate, firm new jars filled with water, maidens, flowers, and goats were set in place here and there.

sanskrit: tathā svalaṃkṛtadvāraṃ nagaraṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ stūyamānaḥ śubhair vākyaiḥ praviveśa suhṛdvṛtaḥ
english: So into the city, its gates finely adorned, the son of Pāṇḍu, praised with auspicious words and surrounded by his friends, made his entry.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca praveśane tu pārthānāṃ janasya puravāsinaḥ didṛkṣūṇāṃ sahasrāṇi samājagmur bahūny atha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the sons of Pṛthā made their entry, many thousands of the city's people, eager for the sight, came thronging together.

sanskrit: sa rājamārgaḥ śuśubhe samalaṃkṛtacatvaraḥ yathā candrodaye rājan vardhamāno mahodadhiḥ
english: That royal road, its squares richly adorned, shone forth, O king, like the great ocean swelling at the rising of the moon.

sanskrit: gṛhāṇi rājamārge tu ratnavanti bṛhanti ca prākampanteva bhāreṇa strīṇāṃ pūrṇāni bhārata
english: The houses along the royal road, jeweled and lofty, seemed to tremble, O Bhārata, with the weight of the women crowding them full.

sanskrit: tāḥ śanair iva savrīḍaṃ praśaśaṃsur yudhiṣṭhiram bhīmasenārjunau caiva mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Softly, as though abashed, those women praised Yudhiṣṭhira, and Bhīmasena and Arjuna, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhanyā tvam asi pāñcāli yā tvaṃ puruṣasattamān upatiṣṭhasi kalyāṇi maharṣīn iva gautamī
english: "Blessed are you, Pāñcālī, who attend, O fair one, upon these best of men, as Gautamī attended upon the great sages.

sanskrit: tava karmāṇy amoghāni vratacaryā ca bhāmini iti kṛṣṇāṃ mahārāja praśaśaṃsus tadā striyaḥ
english: Your deeds are not in vain, nor your keeping of vows, O lovely lady." Thus, O great king, the women then praised Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: praśaṃsāvacanais tāsāṃ mithaḥśabdaiś ca bhārata prītijaiś ca tadā śabdaiḥ puram āsīt samākulam
english: With their words of praise, O Bhārata, and the murmur of voices among them, and the sounds born of their joy, the city was filled with stir.

sanskrit: tam atītya yathāyuktaṃ rājamārgaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ alaṃkṛtaṃ śobhamānam upāyād rājaveśma ha
english: Passing in due order along that royal road, adorned and resplendent, Yudhiṣṭhira drew near to the royal palace.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtayaḥ sarvāḥ paurajānapadās tathā ūcuḥ kathāḥ karṇasukhāḥ samupetya tatas tataḥ
english: Then all the subjects, both townsfolk and country-folk, drawing near from this side and that, spoke words pleasing to the ear:

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jayasi rājendra śatrūñ śatrunisūdana diṣṭyā rājyaṃ punaḥ prāptaṃ dharmeṇa ca balena ca
english: "By good fortune you conquer your foes, O lord of kings, O slayer of enemies; by good fortune the kingdom is regained, through righteousness and through might.

sanskrit: bhava nas tvaṃ mahārāja rājeha śaradāṃ śatam prajāḥ pālaya dharmeṇa yathendras tridivaṃ nṛpa
english: Be you our king here, O great king, for a hundred autumns; guard your subjects in righteousness, O sovereign, as Indra guards the third heaven."

sanskrit: evaṃ rājakuladvāri maṅgalair abhipūjitaḥ āśīrvādān dvijair uktān pratigṛhya samantataḥ
english: Thus honored with auspicious rites at the gate of the royal house, and receiving on every side the blessings uttered by the twice-born,

sanskrit: praviśya bhavanaṃ rājā devarājagṛhopamam śrutvā vijayasaṃyuktaṃ rathāt paścād avātarat
english: the king entered the palace, the likeness of the abode of the king of the gods, and having heard words joined with victory, stepped down from the chariot.

sanskrit: praviśyābhyantaraṃ śrīmān daivatāny abhigamya ca pūjayām āsa ratnaiś ca gandhair mālyaiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Entering within, the glorious one approached the household deities and worshipped them with jewels, with perfumes, and with garlands in every way.

sanskrit: niścakrāma tataḥ śrīmān punar eva mahāyaśāḥ dadarśa brāhmaṇāṃś caiva so 'bhirūpān upasthitān
english: Then the glorious and far-famed one came forth once more and beheld the comely brāhmaṇas standing in attendance.

sanskrit: sa saṃvṛtas tadā viprair āśīrvādavivakṣubhiḥ śuśubhe vimalaś candras tārāgaṇavṛto yathā
english: Surrounded then by the twice-born eager to pronounce their blessings, he shone like the spotless moon ringed about by the host of stars.

sanskrit: tān sa saṃpūjayām āsa kaunteyo vidhivad dvijān dhaumyaṃ guruṃ puraskṛtya jyeṣṭhaṃ pitaram eva ca
english: The son of Kuntī honored those twice-born ones according to rule, placing first his preceptor Dhaumya and his elder father as well.

sanskrit: sumanomodakai ratnair hiraṇyena ca bhūriṇā gobhir vastraiś ca rājendra vividhaiś ca kim icchakaiḥ
english: With flowers and sweetmeats, with jewels and abundant gold, with cattle and garments, O lord of kings, and with sundry things to each one's desire.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇyāhaghoṣo 'bhūd divaṃ stabdhveva bhārata suhṛdāṃ harṣajananaḥ puṇyaḥ śrutisukhāvahaḥ
english: Then arose the proclamation of the holy day, as though propping up the heavens, O Bhārata, sacred, gladdening to friends, and sweet to the ear.

sanskrit: haṃsavan neduṣāṃ rājan dvijānāṃ tatra bhāratī śuśruve vedaviduṣāṃ puṣkalārthapadākṣarā
english: There, O king, the speech of the twice-born who knew the Vedas, sounding like the cry of swans, was heard, rich in meaning, in words, and in syllables.

sanskrit: tato dundubhinirghoṣaḥ śaṅkhānāṃ ca manoramaḥ jayaṃ pravadatāṃ tatra svanaḥ prādurabhūn nṛpa
english: Then the thunder of kettledrums and the delightful sound of conches, the clamor of those who proclaimed victory, broke forth there, O sovereign.

sanskrit: niḥśabde ca sthite tatra tato viprajane punaḥ rājānaṃ brāhmaṇacchadmā cārvāko rākṣaso 'bravīt
english: And when the assembly of the twice-born had fallen silent there once more, the rākṣasa Cārvāka, disguised as a brāhmaṇa, addressed the king.

sanskrit: tatra duryodhanasakhā bhikṣurūpeṇa saṃvṛtaḥ sāṃkhyaḥ śikhī tridaṇḍī ca dhṛṣṭo vigatasādhvasaḥ
english: There the friend of Duryodhana, cloaked in the guise of a mendicant—a Sāṃkhya ascetic, tuft-haired and bearing the triple staff, brazen and devoid of fear—

sanskrit: vṛtaḥ sarvais tadā viprair āśīrvādavivakṣubhiḥ paraṃsahasrai rājendra taponiyamasaṃsthitaiḥ
english: surrounded then by all the twice-born, more than a thousand, eager to pronounce their blessings, steadfast in austerity and restraint, O lord of kings—

sanskrit: sa duṣṭaḥ pāpam āśaṃsan pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām anāmantryaiva tān viprāṃs tam uvāca mahīpatim
english: that wicked one, wishing evil upon the high-souled Pāṇḍavas, without so much as consulting those twice-born ones, spoke thus to the king:

sanskrit: ime prāhur dvijāḥ sarve samāropya vaco mayi dhig bhavantaṃ kunṛpatiṃ jñātighātinam astu vai
english: "All these twice-born ones declare, laying their words upon me: Shame be upon you, a base king, a slayer of your own kin!

sanskrit: kiṃ te rājyena kaunteya kṛtvemaṃ jñātisaṃkṣayam ghātayitvā gurūṃś caiva mṛtaṃ śreyo na jīvitam
english: What good is the kingdom to you, son of Kuntī, having wrought this ruin of your kindred and slain your elders? Death were better than to live."

sanskrit: iti te vai dvijāḥ śrutvā tasya ghorasya rakṣasaḥ vivyathuś cukruśuś caiva tasya vākyapradharṣitāḥ
english: Hearing this from that dreadful rākṣasa, the twice-born ones were sorely shaken and cried out, stung by his words.

sanskrit: tatas te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve sa ca rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vrīḍitāḥ paramodvignās tūṣṇīm āsan viśāṃ pate
english: Then all those brāhmaṇas, and King Yudhiṣṭhira too, abashed and deeply troubled, fell silent, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca prasīdantu bhavanto me praṇatasyābhiyācataḥ pratyāpannaṃ vyasaninaṃ na māṃ dhikkartum arhatha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Be gracious to me, my lords, as I bow and beseech you. I am stricken with calamity and have but now returned; you ought not to reproach me.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājan brāhmaṇās te sarva eva viśāṃ pate ūcur naitad vaco 'smākaṃ śrīr astu tava pārthiva
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, O lord of the people, all those brāhmaṇas said: "This is not our word. May good fortune be yours, O sovereign!"

sanskrit: jajñuś caiva mahātmānas tatas taṃ jñānacakṣuṣā brāhmaṇā vedavidvāṃsas tapobhir vimalīkṛtāḥ
english: And those high-souled brāhmaṇas, knowers of the Vedas, made pure by austerities, then knew him for what he was with the eye of insight.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ eṣa duryodhanasakhā cārvāko nāma rākṣasaḥ parivrājakarūpeṇa hitaṃ tasya cikīrṣati
english: The brāhmaṇas said: This is the friend of Duryodhana, a rākṣasa named Cārvāka, who in the guise of a wandering ascetic seeks to do that one's bidding.

sanskrit: na vayaṃ brūma dharmātman vyetu te bhayam īdṛśam upatiṣṭhatu kalyāṇaṃ bhavantaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: We do not speak thus, O righteous one; let such fear of yours depart. May welfare attend upon you together with your brothers.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve huṃkāraiḥ krodhamūrchitāḥ nirbhartsayantaḥ śucayo nijaghnuḥ pāparākṣasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then all those brāhmaṇas, swollen with wrath, the pure-souled ones, with cries of "huṃ" and with rebukes struck down the wicked rākṣasa.

sanskrit: sa papāta vinirdagdhas tejasā brahmavādinām mahendrāśaninirdagdhaḥ pādapo 'ṅkuravān iva
english: Burnt up by the fiery power of those expounders of the Veda, he fell, like a budding tree scorched by the thunderbolt of great Indra.

sanskrit: pūjitāś ca yayur viprā rājānam abhinandya tam rājā ca harṣam āpede pāṇḍavaḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ
english: Honored, the twice-born departed, having saluted the king; and the king, the Pāṇḍava, with his company of friends, was filled with joy.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca brāhmaṇās tāta loke 'sminn arcanīyāḥ sadā mama ete bhūmicarā devā vāgviṣāḥ suprasādakāḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: The brāhmaṇas, dear one, are ever to be honored by me in this world. These are gods who walk the earth, whose poison is in their speech, yet easily made gracious.

sanskrit: purā kṛtayuge tāta cārvāko nāma rākṣasaḥ tapas tepe mahābāho badaryāṃ bahuvatsaram
english: Long ago, dear one, in the Kṛta age, a rākṣasa named Cārvāka, O mighty-armed one, performed austerities at Badarī for many years.

sanskrit: chandyamāno vareṇātha brahmaṇā sa punaḥ punaḥ abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo varayām āsa bhārata
english: Offered a boon by Brahmā again and again, he chose, O Bhārata, safety from all living beings.

sanskrit: dvijāvamānād anyatra prādād varam anuttamam abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyas tatas tasmai jagatprabhuḥ
english: The Lord of the world then granted him that matchless boon—safety from all beings—save only in the case of contempt for the twice-born.

sanskrit: sa tu labdhavaraḥ pāpo devān amitavikramaḥ rākṣasas tāpayām āsa tīvrakarmā mahābalaḥ
english: But that wicked rākṣasa, having gained the boon, of boundless prowess, fierce in his deeds and mighty in strength, set himself to torment the gods.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sametyātha brahmāṇam idam abruvan vadhāya rakṣasas tasya balaviprakṛtās tadā
english: Then the gods, assembling, sore harried by his might, spoke this to Brahmā, seeking the destruction of that rākṣasa:

sanskrit: tān uvācāvyayo devo vihitaṃ tatra vai mayā yathāsya bhavitā mṛtyur acireṇaiva bhārata
english: The imperishable god said to them: A means has been ordained by me whereby his death shall come about before long, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rājā duryodhano nāma sakhāsya bhavitā nṛpa tasya snehāvabaddho 'sau brāhmaṇān avamaṃsyate
english: A king named Duryodhana shall be his friend, O sovereign; bound by affection for him, this one will hold the brāhmaṇas in contempt.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ ruṣitā viprā viprakārapradharṣitāḥ dhakṣyanti vāgbalāḥ pāpaṃ tato nāśaṃ gamiṣyati
english: Then the twice-born, enraged and provoked by his outrage, mighty in speech, shall burn up the wicked one, and so he shall come to destruction.

sanskrit: sa eṣa nihataḥ śete brahmadaṇḍena rākṣasaḥ cārvāko nṛpatiśreṣṭha mā śuco bharatarṣabha
english: Here lies that rākṣasa Cārvāka, slain by the rod of Brahman, O best of kings; grieve not, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: hatās te kṣatradharmeṇa jñātayas tava pārthiva svargatāś ca mahātmāno vīrāḥ kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ
english: Your kinsmen, O sovereign, were slain by the law of the warrior, and the high-souled heroes, those bulls among kṣatriyas, have gone to heaven.

sanskrit: sa tvam ātiṣṭha kalyāṇaṃ mā te bhūd glānir acyuta śatrūñ jahi prajā rakṣa dvijāṃś ca pratipālaya
english: Therefore stand firm in welfare; let no weariness be yours, O steadfast one. Smite your foes, protect your subjects, and sustain the twice-born.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ kuntīsuto rājā gatamanyur gatajvaraḥ kāñcane prāṅmukho hṛṣṭo nyaṣīdat paramāsane
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, son of Kuntī, his anger gone and his fever gone, glad of heart, sat down facing east upon a supreme golden seat.

sanskrit: tam evābhimukhau pīṭhe sevyāstaraṇasaṃvṛte sātyakir vāsudevaś ca niṣīdatur ariṃdamau
english: Facing him, upon a couch spread with a sumptuous covering, sat the two tamers of foes, Sātyaki and Vāsudeva.
